p: The Packages window (Help → Options → Packages...) manages the data InterSpec reads from files: detector efficiency functions, Isotopics by nuclides presets and report templates, Activity/Shielding Fit report templates, reference spectra, and the knowledge the AI assistant uses. It lets you share them as a single package file, install packages others give you, and choose which item is used when two have the same name.

Drop a package file (.ispkg, or a .zip with an interspec-package.json file at its top level) onto InterSpec, open a .ispkg file with InterSpec (e.g. double-click it, or Open in/Share to InterSpec on a phone or tablet), or use Install a package… on the Installed tab. Before anything is installed, a dialog shows what is in the package, who made it, its handling marking (if any), and a fingerprint (SHA-256) you can compare with whoever sent it. Every item is read the way the tool that uses it reads it, and marked:

ul.li: New, Updated, or Unchanged (when updating a package you already have);
Already installed: an identical item is already available;
Name in use: something you already have has the same name - you choose which one InterSpec uses;
Needs a newer InterSpec: installed, but not used until you upgrade;
Can not be read: installed with the package, but flagged.

p: Items that steer the AI assistant are shown in full, and each must be confirmed before installing. Files that are not a kind InterSpec uses are not installed, and some files are never accepted from a package (for example AI provider settings, which hold API keys, and InterSpec's database).

A package is installed as a whole into its own folder, packages/<name>/ in your user data folder (see Help → About InterSpec → Data); your own files are never changed. Installing a newer version of the same package replaces that folder - the earlier version's files are removed, though its details and change notes are kept, as are your choices and disabled items. To go back to an earlier version, install its package file again. Uninstalling deletes the folder.

When items share a name (a detector efficiency function, a preset, ...), the one looked up by name - by a saved setup, the AI assistant, or batch analysis - is, unless you choose otherwise: your own files, then packages (the one installed first), then InterSpec's own. Lists, like the Detector Efficiency library or the presets menu, show them all, labelled with where they come from. On the By type tab you can choose which one is used, reset that choice, disable an item (hide it from lists and lookups), or delete one of your own files.

On the Create package tab, pick the items to share (your own files, or items from packages you installed - which then record where they came from), fill in the details, and click Check and create. The items are checked first: an item that can not be read, two items with the same name, or files InterSpec never shares, stop the package being made. Then download the package file and give it to others. Making a package does not install it for you; your files stay your own.

To make a new version of a package you made before, choose it under Start from: its details and items are filled in, the version is increased, and items that changed or are no longer found are pointed out. Describe what changed - people updating see the notes of every version since theirs.
A package is a zip file laid out like the user data folder, so you can also make one by hand:

tr.td: Detector efficiency functions: GADRAS folders (Detector.dat + Efficiency.csv), relative-efficiency tables, InterSpec DRF XML, ISOCS and ANGLE files
Activity/Shielding Fit setups (.act.shield.xml), listed in the tool's Preset menu
Activity/Shielding Fit report templates (file names containing tmplt., template., or inja.), and the files they include; also per-file batch reports
Batch Activity/Shielding Fit summary report templates
Batch peak fit report templates, one report per file
Batch peak fit summary report templates
Isotopics by nuclides report templates, also per-file batch reports
Batch Isotopics by nuclides summary report templates
Reference-line sources (.xml, in the format of add_ref_line.xml); read when InterSpec starts
Shielding materials (.txt, in the format of MaterialDataBase.txt); read when InterSpec starts
Nuclide Search categories (.xml, in the format of NuclideSearchCatagories.xml), listed after InterSpec's own
Check-source libraries for Make Detector Response (.lib, in the format of Source.lib)
Color themes (.json, as the Color Themes window exports them)
Reference spectra; each folder in it is one set
AI assistant knowledge: one folder per skill, with a SKILL.md (and optional references/)
AI assistant agent definitions (.xml, in the format of llm_agent_MainAgent.xml); read when InterSpec starts

p: Reference-line sources, shielding materials, Nuclide Search categories, and agents are matched one by one, by name (not file): when a package has one with the same name as one you already have, you choose which is used when installing, and can change it on the By type tab. AI assistant settings (llm_config.xml, llm_tools_config.xml) are never put in, or taken from, a package.
An optional interspec-package.json at the top level describes the package:
pre: { "format_version": 1, "id": "a unique id (a UUID), kept the same for every version", "name": "Field Team HPGe Kit", "version": "3", "author": "...", "organization": "...", "contact": "...", "description": "one line, shown in lists", "notes": "purpose, which detectors or setups, how to use", "changes": "what changed in this version", "handling": "optional marking, e.g. Internal use only", "review_by": "optional date, YYYY-MM-DD", "min_interspec_version": "optional, e.g. 1.0.14", "items": [ { "item_id": "a unique id, kept across versions", "path": "drfs/Detective X.xml", "type": "drf", "sha256": "...", "notes": "...", "intended_override": false } ] }
p: Item types are drf, rel_act_preset, act_shield_setup, act_shield_template, act_shield_summary_template, peak_fit_template, peak_fit_summary_template, isotopics_template, isotopics_summary_template, ref_lines, materials, source_lib, nuc_search_category, color_theme, ref_spectra, llm_skill, and llm_agent. When an item has "intended_override": true and whoever installs the package already has an item of the same name (their own, another package's, or one that comes with InterSpec), the install dialog starts with this one chosen; they can still keep theirs, and nothing is deleted either way. Without this file, the package is installed under the zip file's name, and can not be updated later.
